checks: Checked the statement for integer m≥1, p in [0,1], and independent shape-m scale-one gamma and unit-mean exponential variables. At m=1 the two independent continuous sides are identically distributed for every p, and the endpoint formula equals 1/2. At p=0 only E₁ and E₀ remain. Conditioning on all but E₁ removes ties at every limiting parameter, so coupling and bounded convergence prove continuity at both endpoints.

Independently integrated the survival function for 0<p<1: the integral over u≤x equals (e^(−x)−e^(−x/p))/(1−p), and adding the tail above x gives the stated coefficient p. Evaluating the independent negative-sum Laplace transform at 1 and 1/p gives the stated numerator: the second transform contributes p/(1+p), on top of the survival coefficient p.

At p=1, N(1)=0 and (p²/(1+p))′ at 1 is 3/4, yielding the stated value by the left limit. Independently, Gamma(2,1) survival is e^(−x)(1+x); if H(s)=(1+s)^−1(1+s/m)^−m then H(1)−H′(1)=A(3/4+m/(2(m+1))) gives the same endpoint. For m>1 the difference between the three-term binomial bound for A⁻¹ and (5m+3)/(2(m+1)) is (m−1)/(2m(m+1))>0. Thus P_m(0)>P_m(1) even when the three-term bound itself is exact at m=2.

Recomputed N″ using p²/(1+p)=p−1+1/(1+p). The two terms have positive magnitudes, so the sign of N″ is the sign of R−1. Combining 3/(1+p)−(m+2)/(m+p) gives the positive numerator (m−1)(2−p), and N″(1)=A[m/(2(m+1))−1/4]>0 for m>1. If R(0)≥1 take c=0, including equality at zero; otherwise continuity and strict increase give the unique c in (0,1) with R(c)=1.

Subtracting the affine term gives Q(1)=Q′(1)=0 and Q(0)>0. Integration from one twice yields the stated sign and kernel (t−p). For p≥c and p<1 the integrand is strictly positive in the open integration interval. If c>0, concavity on [0,c] gives a strictly positive chord lower bound. Division by 1−p is used only for p<1; the separately established p=0 and p=1 values complete the equality criterion.

overlap.comparison: For k=1 the interior stationary exclusion concerns p≤b=p/m, which forces m=1. It shares the symmetry case, but leaves p>b for every interior p when m>1 and therefore gives neither the finite-m endpoint minimum nor its equality condition.
Its classification of minimizers identifies the capped interior stratum with b=p/m for k=1. It does not compare the values of that stratum with its endpoints.

When p=1, k=2 saturated positives and q=m residual phases identify the same equal-negative law as the fixed-q saturated minimum. That theorem assumes saturated positives and does not compare p<1 to this law.

Its k=1 saturated case gives 1/2 for zero residual coefficients, as at p=0. Its k=2 fixed-q minimum is the p=1 law, but the result varies q within saturated laws, rather than comparing all p at fixed m.
It describes the same finite signed family before taking a limit and computes an m→∞ limit at fixed k. A limit does not compare P_m(p) and P_m(1) at finite m.

The positive merge transfers weight at fixed positive and negative totals, whereas changing p here changes the total and residual negatives. Its generic lower bound cannot imply the sharp value even at p=1, where its first lower bound is strict for two positive phases.
The deterministic-threshold reduction yields a uniform lower bound from an all-k, all-p premise, not the finite-m endpoint value or a comparison to it.
